# Raster manipulation with terra vs stars packages

Overall difference between stars and terra found [here](https://eds-223-geospatial.github.io/course-materials/discussions/week4-v2-discussion.html#terra-vs.-stars-whats-the-difference)

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(spDataLarge)
library(sf)
library(stars)
library(terra)
```


# Data

Digital elevation model (DEM) of Mt. Mongón, Perú, obtained from spDataLarge
Landsat image of Zion National Park, obtained from spDataLarge
SRTM elevation of Zion National Park, obtained from spDataLarge

## Terra

```{r}
dem <- terra::rast(system.file("raster/dem.tif", package = "spDataLarge"))
landsat <- terra::rast(system.file("raster/landsat.tif", package = "spDataLarge"))
srtm <- terra::rast(system.file("raster/srtm.tif", package = "spDataLarge"))
```

## Stars

```{r}
dem_s <- stars::read_stars(system.file("raster/dem.tif", package = "spDataLarge"))
landsat_s <- stars::read_stars(system.file("raster/landsat.tif", package = "spDataLarge"))
srtm_s <- stars::read_stars(system.file("raster/srtm.tif", package = "spDataLarge"))
```

# Explore elevation at Mt. Mongón, Perú

Make a boxplot and histogram of elevation at Mt. Mongón, Perú

## Terra

```{r}
# For terra package
terra::hist(dem,
            main = 'Digital Elevation Model Distribution',
            xlab = 'Value')

terra::boxplot(dem,
            main = 'Digital Elevation Model Distribution',
            xlab = 'Value')
```

boxplot - `dem` mean is about 480. The max value is above 1000 and lowest is about 200.
histogram - right scewed with most values around 400

## Stars

```{r}
# Same but with stars package
dem_values <- as.vector(dem_s[[1]]) # dem[[1]] pulls out the first attribute: a plain R matrix of elevation. as.vector() flattens the matrix into one long numeric vactor

hist(dem_values,
    main = 'Digital Elevation Model Distribution',
    xlab = 'Value')

boxplot(dem_values, ylab = 'Value')
```

Reclassify dem and compute the mean for the three classes:
Low, where elevation is less than 300
Medium
High, where elevation is greater than 500

## Terra

```{r}
# For terra package
# Define a reclassification matrix
rcl <- matrix(c(-Inf, 300, 0, # values -Inf to 300 = 0
                300, 500, 1,  # values 300 to 500 = 1
                500, Inf, 2), # values 500 to Inf = 2
                ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE) # True fills the matrix row by row, so each line of code reads as one rule

# Apply the matrix to reclassify the raster, making all cells 0 or 1 or 2
dem_rcl <- terra::classify(dem, rcl = rcl)

# New version: a plain data.frame works with both older and newer terra
levels(dem_rcl) <- data.frame(id = 0:2,
                              cats = c("low", "medium", "high"))

# Calculate mean elevation for each category using original DEM values
elevation_mean <- terra::zonal(dem, dem_rcl, fun = "mean") # zonal() smmarise one raster's values inside zones set by another raster. dem supplies the values, dem_rcl supplies the zones
elevation_mean
```

## Stars

```{r}
# Same but with stars package
# Reclassify by cutting values into intervals, returning a factor raster
dem_rcl <- cut(dem_s,
               breaks = c(-Inf, 300, 500, Inf), # -Inf to 300, 300 to 500, 500 to Inf
               labels = c("low", "medium", "high"))

plot(dem_rcl, main = "Reclassified elevation")

# Calculate mean elevation for each category using original DEM values
elevation_mean <- tibble(elevation = as.vector(dem[[1]]),
                         cats = factor(as.vector(dem_rcl[[1]]), levels = levels(dem_rcl[[1]]))) %>%
  group_by(cats) %>%
  summarise(mean_elevation = mean(elevation, na.rm = TRUE))
elevation_mean
```



# Explore NDVI and NDWI at Zion National Park

Calculate the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) at Zion National Park
Calculate the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) at Zion National Park
Find a correlation between NDVI and NDWI at Zion National Park


## Terra

```{r}
scale_factor <- 0.0000275
offset <- 0.2

scale_function <- function(x) {
  x * scale_factor + offset
}

landsat_scaled <- terra::app(landsat, fun = scale_function)
```

```{r}
ndwi_fun <- function(green, nir){
    (green - nir)/(green + nir)
}

ndvi_fun <- function(nir, red){
  (nir - red)/(nir + red)
}
```

```{r}
ndwi_rast <- terra::lapp(landsat_scaled[[c(2, 4)]],
                         fun = ndwi_fun)

ndvi_rast <- terra::lapp(landsat_scaled[[c(4, 3)]],
                         fun = ndvi_fun)
```

```{r}
plot(ndwi_rast,
     main = "Zion National Park NDWI")
```

```{r}
combine <- c(ndvi_rast, ndwi_rast) # Stack rasters

plot(combine, main = c("NDVI", "NDWI")) # Plot
```

```{r}
# Calculate correlation between raster layers
terra::layerCor(combine, fun = cor)
```

## Stars
```{r}
# Same but with stars
scale_factor <- 0.0000275
offset <- 0.2

# Arithmetic on a stars object is applied to every grid cell
landsat_scaled <- landsat_s * scale_factor + offset
```

```{r}
ndwi_fun <- function(green, nir){
    (green - nir)/(green + nir)
}

ndvi_fun <- function(nir, red){
  (nir - red)/(nir + red)
}
```

```{r}
# Split the "band" dimension into attributes (X1 = blue, X2 = green, X3 = red, X4 = NIR)
landsat_bands <- split(landsat_scaled, "band")
landsat_bands
```

```{r}
ndwi_rast <- landsat_bands %>%
  transmute(ndwi = ndwi_fun(green = X2, nir = X4))

ndvi_rast <- landsat_bands %>%
  transmute(ndvi = ndvi_fun(nir = X4, red = X3))
```

```{r}
plot(ndwi_rast,
     main = "Zion National Park NDWI")
```

```{r}
plot(ndvi_rast,
     main = "Zion National Park NDVI")
```

```{r}
combine <- c(ndvi_rast, ndwi_rast) # Combine as two attributes

plot(merge(combine)) # Merge attributes into a dimension to plot side by side
```

```{r}
# Calculate correlation between the two attributes
cor(as.vector(combine$ndvi), as.vector(combine$ndwi), use = "complete.obs")
```


# Change resolution of elevation at Zion National Park

Use all the methods available to change the resolution of elevation at Zion National Park to 0.01 by 0.01 degrees

## Terra

```{r}
plot(srtm)
```

```{r}
rast_template <- terra::rast(terra::ext(srtm), res = 0.01) # Create empty template
```

```{r}
srtm_resampl1 <- terra::resample(srtm, y = rast_template, method = "bilinear")
srtm_resampl2 <- terra::resample(srtm, y = rast_template, method = "near")
srtm_resampl3 <- terra::resample(srtm, y = rast_template, method = "cubic")
srtm_resampl4 <- terra::resample(srtm, y = rast_template, method = "cubicspline")
srtm_resampl5 <- terra::resample(srtm, y = rast_template, method = "lanczos")
```

```{r}
srtm_resampl_all <- c(srtm_resampl1, srtm_resampl2, srtm_resampl3, srtm_resampl4, srtm_resampl5)
labs <- c("Bilinear", "Near", "Cubic", "Cubic Spline", "Lanczos")

plot(srtm_resampl_all, main = labs)
```

## Stars

```{r}
plot(srtm_s)
```


```{r}
# Create empty template from the bounding box of srtm
rast_template <- stars::st_as_stars(sf::st_bbox(srtm_s), dx = 0.01, dy = 0.01)
```


```{r}
# use_gdal = TRUE is needed for methods other than nearest neighbor
srtm_resampl1 <- stars::st_warp(srtm_s, dest = rast_template, method = "bilinear", use_gdal = TRUE, no_data_value = -9999)
srtm_resampl2 <- stars::st_warp(srtm_s, dest = rast_template, method = "near", use_gdal = TRUE, no_data_value = -9999)
srtm_resampl3 <- stars::st_warp(srtm_s, dest = rast_template, method = "cubic", use_gdal = TRUE, no_data_value = -9999)
srtm_resampl4 <- stars::st_warp(srtm_s, dest = rast_template, method = "cubicspline", use_gdal = TRUE, no_data_value = -9999)
srtm_resampl5 <- stars::st_warp(srtm_s, dest = rast_template, method = "lanczos", use_gdal = TRUE, no_data_value = -9999)
```


```{r}
srtm_resampl_all <- c(srtm_resampl1, srtm_resampl2, srtm_resampl3, srtm_resampl4, srtm_resampl5)
names(srtm_resampl_all) <- c("Bilinear", "Near", "Cubic", "Cubic Spline", "Lanczos")

plot(merge(srtm_resampl_all))
```
